iconicAnchor.label: 50 Years of Helvetica exhibition
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Neo-grotesk typography in modern graphic design
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: MoMA's exhibition connects neutral, well-proportioned sans letterforms to posters, signage, and other modern graphic applications.

sources.title: 50 Years of Helvetica
supports: Neutral, well-proportioned neo-grotesk letterforms communicate modern clarity across many applications.
The type family supports a broad hierarchy rather than a novelty display effect.

sources.title: HelveticaSpecimenCH.svg
supports: The audited specimen documents neutral grotesk proportions and weight relationships.
It is contextual evidence for typography, not sufficient visual evidence of editorial pacing by itself.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches neo grotesk, measured hierarchy, flush left, editorial pace, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/neo-grotesk-editorial/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
